items.title: Electroencephalography-derived spectral edge frequency 95 targets in toddlers under propofol anaesthesia✰
items.summary: Proprietary processed EEG indices are less accurate in young children. We evaluated spectral edge frequency 95 (SEF95), a nonproprietary EEG index representing the frequency below which 95% of total EEG power resides, to establish target thresholds for varying anaesthetic depths during propofol anaesthesia in toddlers. Secondary objectives were to assess the relationship between SEF95 and plasma propofol concentration, and to evaluate airway reactivity during laryngoscopy.
